assignedTask.title: [Agent trial] Maintainer assignment: preserve SIGINT child exit status in cage relay
assignedTask.body:
Maintainer-assigned real engineering task for the resident. This is not external adoption feedback.

Observed on the current source: src/cage/relay.js exits with 143 when its child terminates with SIGINT. The relay's stated contract is to leave with the child's exit status; the conventional shell status for SIGINT is 128 + 2 = 130.

Reproduction (run from the repository, Node on Linux/macOS):

```js
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
const result = spawnSync(process.execPath, [
  'src/cage/relay.js', '/tmp/unused-agenthub-task.sock', '0', '--',
  process.execPath, '-e', "process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGINT')"
], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 5000 });
console.log(result.status); // observed 143; expected 130
```

The unused Unix socket is never contacted by this reproduction. Port 0 requests an ephemeral loopback port. No external service or credentials are needed.

Acceptance:
- Independently reproduce the baseline failure with a new regression test.
- Correct source behavior without editing existing tests, the controller, workflows or manifests.
- Preserve ordinary numeric child exit codes, SIGTERM=143 and SIGKILL=137.
- The exact regression must fail before the change and pass after it; the complete existing suite must pass.
- Save a candidate branch/PR with actual execution evidence. Do not claim success from a proposed patch or model review.

Start with src/cage/relay.js. Do not pursue the earlier unverified port-binding-race hypothesis for this task. If blocked, record the actual tool error and checkpoint.

This task tests one useful repair, not autonomous general intelligence or adoption.

opportunities.title: MCP OAuth URL rejected as credential (fixed_credential_raw false positive on 144-char client_id) blocks Sweet Security MCP
opportunities.excerpt:
Environment: Kiro Crew (Windows), kiro-cli 3.2.0
MCP server: sweet, https://eapi.sweet.security/docs/mcp (OAuth)

## Steps
1. Add the sweet MCP server and start the connection (OAuth).
2. The dashboard refuses to show the approval address because it "contains credential-like data".

## gateway.log (2026-11-26 17:02:20)
```
WARNING kiro_crew.security.exfil: OAuth URL rejected rule=fixed_credential_raw component=query_parameter parameter=client_id length=144 upper=60 lower=57 digits=26 percent=0 symbols=1 other=0
WARNING kiro_crew.dashboard.chat_runner: ACP: rejecting MCP OAuth URL with credential/exfil pattern for sweet
```

## Expected
The OAuth authorize URL opens. client_id is a public identifier, not a secret.

## Actual
The URL is rejected, so the server stays in "waiting for a person to sign in" and cannot connect.

## Notes
- credential_redaction is not the cause. The block comes from the exfil gate (_contains_fixed_credential), which stays active when redaction is off.
- oauth_endpoints.json already lists Sweet's /app/authorize. The error persisted after a gateway restart.

## Request
Exempt OAuth client_id (and other public OAuth params such as state and code_challenge) from the fixed_credential_raw check, or add an owner-approved allowlist per MCP server/domain.

opportunities.title: Claude Code adapter: a trust dialog that warns of hooks in .claude/skills or .claude/agents is not recognised
opportunities.excerpt:
Found in the review of #848 (#752), reproduced with Claude Code 2.1.332. Not changed there.

A repository whose skill, command or agent declares hooks in its front matter gets a folder-trust dialog with the hooks warning, naming a directory and not a settings file, and no line naming files:

```
 Claude Code'll be able to read, edit, and execute files here.

 ⚠ This folder configures hooks that can run commands without asking, declared
 in .claude/skills

 Security guide

 ❯ No, exit
   Yes, I trust this folder
```

(`.claude/skills` with a `.claude/skills/x/SKILL.md`, `.claude/agents` with a `.claude/agents/x.md`; by the program text also `.claude/commands`, and together with the settings files.)

The adapter reads the hooks warning only when the line "Trusting this folder loads" names what it declares, so this screen gets no key and no event: the start ends at the start timeout with raw terminal output. No `trust_files` entry helps, and a person is not told that hooks are why. In a confined session the dialog has no warning and is answered.

By the program text (not reproduced), a dialog for the home folder says one more sentence, "This is your home folder, so Yes lasts for this session only.", and is not read either.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Real captures of the dialog whose warning names `.claude/skills` and `.claude/agents`, alone and with a settings file, are read: refused naming them, or answered when all are trusted, as the owner decides for what `trust_files` may name. The tests fail on main.
- [ ] Any other directory there, or any other text, gets no key.

Related: #592, #752, #758.

Observed on the current source: src/cage/relay.js exits with 143 when its child terminates with SIGINT. The relay's stated contract is to leave with the child's exit status; the conventional shell status for SIGINT is 128 + 2 = 130.

Reproduction (run from the repository, Node on Linux/macOS):

```js
import { spawnSync } from 'node:child_process';
const result = spawnSync(process.execPath, [
  'src/cage/relay.js', '/tmp/unused-agenthub-task.sock', '0', '--',
  process.execPath, '-e', "process.kill(process.pid, 'SIGINT')"
], { encoding: 'utf8', timeout: 5000 });
console.log(result.status); // observed 143; expected 130
```

The unused Unix socket is never contacted by this reproduction. Port 0 requests an ephemeral loopback port. No external service or credentials are needed.

Acceptance:
- Independently reproduce the baseline failure with a new regression test.
- Correct source behavior without editing existing tests, the controller, workflows or manifests.
- Preserve ordinary numeric child exit codes, SIGTERM=143 and SIGKILL=137.
- The exact regression must fail before the change and pass after it; the complete existing suite must pass.
- Save a candidate branch/PR with actual execution evidence. Do not claim success from a proposed patch or model review.

Start with src/cage/relay.js. Do not pursue the earlier unverified port-binding-race hypothesis for this task. If blocked, record the actual tool error and checkpoint.

This task tests one useful repair, not autonomous general intelligence or adoption.
